changes.current: The exact factor product is \[ LR^* = Q_LGQ_R^*. \] The two outer maps are isometries on their column spaces. They preserve the nonzero singular values and the spectral and Frobenius norms of the core. For every ambient rank-at-most-$k$ competitor $B$, its compression $Q_L^*BQ_R$ has rank at most $k$, and compression cannot increase either norm. Thus the core best-approximation inequality also lower-bounds the error of every ambient competitor. Truncating the singular value decomposition of \(G\) and applying \cref{fact:eym} gives the result. The compact QR dimensions equal the ranks of the factor column spaces.

changes.current: The recursive level of a vertex is one plus the largest level of its predecessors. For a nonempty graph, the largest level therefore counts the vertices on a longest path. For an empty graph, no task is scheduled and the depth is zero.

changes.current: The Karush Kuhn Tucker conditions give the unconstrained form on every nonactive coordinate and equality with \(m_e\) on every active upper bound. The weighted sum \[ \phi(\lambda) = \sum_es_e \min\left\{ m_e, \frac{c_e}{\lambda s_e} \right\} \] is continuous and nonincreasing. It decreases from the maximal feasible value to zero. For a strictly submaximal budget, once any coordinate is unsaturated, $\phi$ is strictly decreasing, which gives a unique multiplier. At maximal budget the only feasible vector is $(m_e)_e$ and every $0<\lambda\le\min_e c_e/(s_em_e)$ produces it. Thus the minimizing vector is unique at this endpoint while its multiplier need not be. Strict convexity gives uniqueness of the minimizer in every case.
